newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares close with slight gain, poll weighs.
newsitem.headline: French shares close with slight gain, poll weighs.

text.p: French shares closed with a small gain on Thursday after a rumour, later confirmed, of an opinion poll giving the centre-right a small majority after the election, dealers said.
The market had been on the look-out for opinion polls, having had only a quick CSA poll of Tuesday which saw the ruling coalition maintaining a majority, albeit reduced.
IPSOS, retained by Le Point weekly, showed the centre-right would win 292 seats, the Socialists 256 and the Communists 28 -- giving the centre-right an eight-seat majority over the left.

"The market is very thin and will go up and down according to the opinion polls. That may seem ridiculous but that's how it is," a broker said. "It is not a market in which investors want to have an open position."

The market had been supported most of the day by a firmer dollar, the start of the May bourse account, a higher opening on Wall Street and a technical attempt to break the 2,550 level in the futures market.
In the afternoon, after that resistance level was breached, the CAC rose more than one percent. But the poll rumour deflated the rally.
Dealers were unsure whether the poll would weigh on the market on Friday as well, adding that Wall Street was still a big influence.
One broker said the pending election and a string of holidays in May left him feeling cautious on the May account. "Sell in May and go away," he said, citing a bourse proverb.
* The CAC-40 index closed up 0.24 percent at 2539.83 while the April future ended two points higher at 2,538. But on GLOBEX it was down six at 2,530 in after-hours trading at 1540 GMT.
* Volume was 5.3 billion francs, of which 4.2 billion in blue-chip CAC shares.

* AGF, up 0.71 percent at 184.90 francs, told Reuters it could look into buying the insurance activities of GAN, up 2.13 percent at 153.20 francs, if they were put up for sale. The market had been speculating about a possible bid.

* Rhone-Poulenc, up 2.74 percent at 187.50 francs, rose after its pharmaceuticals unit Rhone-Poulenc Rorer, up 2.21 percent at 410.90 francs, said it could buy back up to five million shares. Rhone was also helped by its chairman's remarks on Wednesday that there could be an additional two billion francs of asset sales in 1997.
* Eurotunnel, unchanged at 6.50 francs, had been up most of the day on the back of a debt restructuring deal with a bank steering committee.
* L'Oreal, up 2.25 percent at 1,951, extended its gains on its results outlook. Morgan Stanley increased its price target to 2,170 francs from 2,100.
* Accor, down 2.60 percent at 860 francs, was hit by profit-taking on strong recent gains.
* Suez, up 0.65 percent at 277 francs, said it would sell its SEV stake to Commercial Union. CU said the stake's valuation at year's end was about 90 million pounds.
